status: RATIFIED as built on 2026-11-02 (five-section thank-you structure; see structure_approval). The owner supplied no precise thank-you layout (82-signature-thank-you/references/layout-and-copy-profiles.md, preamble). This spec merges the two structures already in the repo: Skill 82's order of parts (header, order summary, access blocks, what happens next, support and manage) and Skill 49's TY bands (a welcome, 4 to 6 numbered next steps, a signed close of up to 170 characters, no offer button, exactly one celebration hero image). It is the page type's canonical section sequence for the Skill 71 pipeline, in the same shape as the landing specs, so the section-count check, the request builder, the wireframe prompt and the copy validator read it through scripts/page_role.py and never fork the pipeline. Change this file, not the code, when Trevor changes the layout.

structure_approval.basis: Decision taken as recommended on 2026-11-02 (repair project bfl-s49-repair-20261102, decision STR-17): ratify as built, because the structure already matches Skill 49 page_types, Skill 71 copy specs and funnel_structure.json. A later change to its sections is a new decision with its own date.

later_decisions.basis: A new dated decision under the rule above, not a change to the ratified five-section sequence. Section 2 is one summary card holding only the copy's approved item line and payment line (no table, column headers, status chips, grey bars or totals). Section 3 draws one card per item the copy names. Section 5 draws a filled support button, an outlined button with the copy's own label and a signature line, with no grey bar.

A new dated decision under the rule above, not a change to the ratified five-section sequence. Section 2's heading is the section heading of the closed export (copy/public-copy.md, `## What you purchased`): the request builder puts it first in the section's verbatim copy (`copy_heading`), its lines carry the roles H2, Body, Body (`line_roles`), so the sheet prints one H2 heading and no subhead, and the section's colour paragraph (`wireframe_colour`) spends no accent fill. The grey name tab of the sheet grammar still reads the section name, ORDER SUMMARY, and nowhere else do those words print.

A new dated decision under the rule above, not a change to the ratified five-section sequence. The page's one celebration image slot (TY-IMG-01, section 1) is 1:1, the ratio the closed image inventory records for it (desktop-wireframe/image-inventory.json, IMG-001), not the 4:3 this spec carried; a request slot and its closed inventory entry must agree, and the section plan writer (scripts/write_section_plan.py) refuses a request that plans another ratio than the inventory. Style B's circle slot was already 1:1.

guide.note: Skill 82 owns the page's truth (purchase records, access, billing). This spec owns its section sequence and picture layout for the wireframe and mockup stages. The copy for the page comes from Skill 82's clean copy profiles; it is never invented here.

counting_convention.word_tokenization: Strip markers, normalize whitespace, count whitespace-separated tokens.
counting_convention.source: Same convention as the landing specs (standard-v6.json counting_convention).

rules.primary_button: the access button, filled in the client's primary brand colour
rules.no_pitch: The page sells nothing: no new offer, no price for anything not purchased, no 'one more thing' (82-signature-thank-you/references/no-pitch-policy.md).
rules.source: Skill 49 structure/funnel_structure.json (thank_you, image_coverage.page_policies.thank-you: one celebratory hero, image maximum of one; profiles.thank-you: no offer CTAs); Skill 82 no-pitch policy.

cta_map.note: Utility buttons only (access, download, schedule, support). Never an offer button. Section 3 shows one card as the pattern and repeats once per purchased item.

sections.name: Confirmation and welcome
sections.job: Celebrate the decision and confirm the order honestly: a status label and headline, one reassurance line, the primary access button and the order reference, beside the page's one celebration image.

cta.note: The primary access button ('Start here'); absent only when no access is granted yet.

limits.source: Skill 49 TY-1 band (120 to 180 characters), applied as a suggestion because the headline states the real order status

default_slots.art_direction: warm celebration of the decision, a confident moment for the buyer, never a product pitch

layout.desktop: Hero ground band inside the 1200 px content column. The text block, top to bottom: a status label chip, the page headline (H1) stating the order status honestly, one reassurance line, the primary access button (filled, primary brand colour) and under it the order reference in small tracked capitals. The page's one celebration image plate is composed with the treatment the composition contract names for the slot; whatever that treatment, the text block keeps this order and the button stays filled in the primary colour. Spacing and type: about 96 px of padding above and below the band; roughly 24 px between the status label chip and the headline, 16 px between the headline and the reassurance line, 32 px before the button and 16 px between the button and the order reference. The headline takes the largest type size on the page, two lines at most, left-aligned in the brand display face; the reassurance line is body size on one or two lines; the status label chip is a small tag in tracked capitals carrying only the copy's own status word. The button is one filled rectangle at least 48 px tall with the copy's label centred; the order reference is plain muted text without a border or a fill. The text column and the image plate split the band at roughly 55 and 45 percent with a 48 px gutter, the plate top-aligned to the first line of the text block, and the corner treatment of every element follows the client's design style.
layout.mobile: Single-column phone stack: the text block in the same order (status label chip, headline, reassurance line, primary access button, order reference), with the celebration image plate placed where the composition contract places it; the primary access button spans the full content column. Spacing and type: about 48 px of padding above and below the band with 20 px side gutters; 16 px between the status label chip and the headline, 12 px under the headline, 24 px before the button and 12 px between the button and the order reference. The headline wraps to three lines at most and stays left-aligned; the status label chip keeps its tracked capitals at a legible small size; the button is at least 48 px tall so a thumb can hit it; the order reference stays on one line of plain muted text. The image plate keeps the ratio its slot declares and is never cropped into a banner strip.

sections.note: Primary access button sits under the headline and reassurance line; order reference is text, never a button

sections.name: Order summary
sections.job: Summarise the purchase from the approved copy only: the section's closed heading, then one summary card that holds the copy's approved item line and the copy's approved payment line as readable text.
sections.wireframe_colour: COLOUR — every colour comes from the BRAND COLORS line in this prompt, the client's own resolved palette. In this section the primary colour fills the section chip only: the section has no button and no image plate, and its heading and card text are set in the one brand text colour with no primary-colour or accent fill on any word. The lightest brand colours are the light grounds and the card differs from its ground by tone. The sheet is never grey line work on a pale ground, never colourless and never outline-only: the chip carries the brand colour. Do not borrow a colour from the style reference or from any other client.

layout.desktop: Light ground band. The section heading, which is the first line of the copy block and prints once, then ONE summary card inside the 1200 px content column. The card holds only the copy's approved item line and the copy's approved payment line, set as readable text. No table, no column headers, no status labels, no grey bars, no totals, no image and no button. Nothing the copy does not supply is drawn: never an item name, a figure or a currency sign that the approved copy does not carry. Spacing and type: about 80 px of padding above and below the band; the section heading sits 32 px above the card, left-aligned in the display face at the second-largest size on the page. The card is a single surface with a hairline border and 32 px of inner padding, centred in the column and no wider than about 880 px so the lines stay short and readable. Inside, the approved item line is set first at body size and the approved payment line under it, 16 px apart, both left-aligned in the body face with a line height of about 1.5. The card surface differs from the light band ground by tone, not by shadow. The words are exactly the approved copy lines, wrapped naturally; nothing is abbreviated, reordered or recast into columns, and the corner treatment follows the client's design style. Text handling: only the page's display and body faces appear, with no new face introduced. The item line may wrap onto as many lines as it needs and the payment line is never merged into it, even when both are short; alignment stays left across the card, never centred or justified. The band's top and bottom edges butt directly against the neighbouring bands with no gap, divider ornament or shadow between them. Colour use is restrained: the heading and card text take the page's dark text colour, the hairline border takes the neutral rule colour, and no accent colour is spent in this section.
layout.mobile: Light ground band. The section heading, which is the first line of the copy block and prints once, then ONE summary card at full width, holding only the copy's approved item line and the copy's approved payment line as readable text. No table, no column headers, no status labels, no grey bars, no totals, no image and no button. Nothing the copy does not supply is drawn: never an item name, a figure or a currency sign that the approved copy does not carry. Spacing and type: about 48 px of padding above and below the band with 20 px side gutters; the section heading sits 24 px above the card. The card runs the full content width with 24 px of inner padding and a hairline border; the item line is set first and the payment line under it, 12 px apart, left-aligned at body size with a line height of about 1.5, so every word wraps and none is cut off or shortened with an ellipsis. Nothing sits beside the card, and the card's height follows its text. Text handling: the heading and both lines use the page's body and display faces only, with no new face introduced. The item line may be long, so it is allowed to wrap onto as many lines as it needs, and the payment line is never merged into the item line, even when both are short. Alignment stays left across the card, never centred or justified, so the ragged right edge reads cleanly at phone width. The card sits on the light ground with a clear 20 px of ground visible on both sides, and the band's top and bottom edges butt directly against the neighbouring bands with no gap, divider ornament or shadow between them. Colour use is restrained: the heading and the card text take the page's dark text colour, the hairline border takes the neutral rule colour, and no accent colour is spent in this section, which keeps the confirmation calm and the access section below it the first place the accent returns with force. A reader should be able to read both lines at arm's length on a phone without zooming, so neither line drops below the body size of the page.

sections.note: Summary from the approved copy only

sections.name: Access
sections.job: Give one access card per purchased item: its name, what it unlocks, and one utility button that goes to it.

cta.note: One access, download or schedule button per card; the manuscript shows one card as the pattern.

layout.desktop: Dark ground band. A section heading, then a row of access cards across the 1200 px column, one card per item the copy names. Each card: an icon at the top from the brand's icon style, the item name from the copy, one line saying what it unlocks, and one filled utility button carrying the copy's own label. No photograph. Draw only the cards the copy names: no placeholder card, no grey bar and no invented product, bonus or membership. Spacing and type: about 80 px of padding above and below the band; the section heading sits 40 px above the card row, left-aligned in the display face and set in light type on the dark ground. Cards sit on a 24 px gap and share one height with 28 px of inner padding; one, two or three cards fill the row, and a single card is centred at no more than about 560 px wide rather than stretched across the column. Inside each card, top to bottom: the icon at about 48 px, 20 px of space, the item name in the heading face, 8 px of space, the one-line description at body size in a muted light tone, then 24 px of space before the button, which is pinned to the card's bottom edge so the buttons align across cards. One icon family with one line weight and size is used on every card, drawn in the brand accent colour; card surfaces differ from the dark ground by a lighter tone and a hairline border, not by a shadow, and light type on the dark ground keeps the brand's readable-contrast floor. Text handling: item names use the heading face one step below the section heading and wrap as needed; descriptions are set on one line where the card allows and wrap to a second otherwise, never truncated; button labels are the copy's own words, centred, and never shortened. The icon sits in a square slot of fixed size so item names align from card to card. Cards never overlap, never scroll sideways and never collapse into a carousel, and every card the copy names is visible at once in the order the copy lists them. The band's top and bottom edges butt directly against the neighbouring bands with no gap or ornament.
layout.mobile: Dark ground band. The cards stack one per row at full width, one card per item the copy names, each with its icon, item name, one-line description and a full-width utility button carrying the copy's own label. No photograph. Draw only the cards the copy names: no placeholder card, no grey bar and no invented product, bonus or membership. Spacing and type: about 48 px of padding above and below the band with 20 px side gutters; the section heading sits 24 px above the first card in light type, left-aligned. Cards are 16 px apart with 20 px of inner padding; in each, the icon at about 40 px sits at the left of the item name on one line, the one-line description follows 8 px under it and the full-width button follows 16 px under that, at least 48 px tall. A card's height follows its text, so a longer item name wraps to a second line rather than being cut off. The icon family, accent colour, hairline border and lighter card surface match the desktop cards, and the cards keep the item order the copy gives. Text handling: item names use the heading face at a size one step below the section heading and wrap to as many lines as they need; descriptions stay on one line where the column allows and wrap to a second line otherwise, never truncated. Button labels are the copy's own words, set in the button face at the brand's button size, centred, and never shortened to fit. The icon is decorative: it sits in a square slot of fixed size so the item names align from card to card, and it is drawn from the brand's icon style rather than from a stock set, with a line weight matching the type's stroke. Cards never overlap, never scroll sideways and never collapse into a carousel; every card the copy names is visible at once in the order the copy lists them. The band's top and bottom edges butt directly against the neighbouring bands with no gap or ornament, and light type on the dark ground holds the brand's readable-contrast floor for both the item name and the description. An item the copy marks as pending or failed gets no card, and no card is added for anything the copy does not name.

sections.note: One card per item the copy names; no card for a pending or failed item

sections.name: What happens next
sections.job: Say in four to six numbered steps what happens now and next, momentum-ordered, each step starting with a verb and naming its payoff.

step_count.source: Skill 49 TY-2 (4 to 6 numbered steps; each step 89 to 116 characters, applied by the reviewer: per-step character bands are defined for a seven-step page only)

layout.desktop: Light ground band. A section heading, then the numbered steps inside the 1200 px column, drawn in the client's design style: Style A (Block) runs them as full-width numbered rows, one step per row, a primary-colour square-cornered number block at the left of each row and a hairline rule between rows; Style B (Circle) and Style C (Hybrid) set them in one horizontal row of primary-colour circle badges joined by a dotted line, with the verb-led step label under each. No button and no image. Spacing and type: about 80 px of padding above and below the band; the section heading sits 40 px above the steps, left-aligned in the display face. Each step shows its number once, in the brand display face inside the number marker the design style names, with the step text at body size beside it, no more than three lines, and the verb that opens the step set in the heading weight so the eye reads the action first. Steps sit 24 px apart and keep the order the copy gives; the numbers climb from 1 to the last step with none skipped or repeated. Text handling: a connecting rule or dotted line runs behind the markers where the design style calls for one and never crosses the step text; the band's top and bottom edges butt directly against the neighbouring bands with no gap, and the section stays free of any decorative image, icon or call to action.
layout.mobile: Light ground band. The steps stack in one column at full width, each number badge beside its step label: square-cornered number blocks with hairline rules between rows for Style A, primary-colour circle badges on a dotted line down the left for Style B and Style C. No button and no image. Spacing and type: about 48 px of padding above and below the band with 20 px side gutters; the section heading sits 24 px above the first step. Each marker is about 40 px across, the step text beside it wraps within the column up to four lines, and steps sit 20 px apart. The opening verb of each step takes the heading weight, and the numbers climb from 1 to the last step once each. Text handling: step text is set at body size with the opening verb in the heading weight and wraps freely within the column; a connecting rule or dotted line runs behind the markers where the design style calls for one and never crosses the step text. The band's top and bottom edges butt directly against the neighbouring bands with no gap, and the section stays free of any decorative image, icon or call to action.

sections.note: Four to six steps; badges read 1 to N once each, in order; no button here

sections.name: Help, manage and close
sections.job: Close the page: one help line that says how to get help with this order and carries the support email address, the one filled support button, and a short signed note of thanks of up to 170 characters. No offer button.

cta.note: One filled support button, the only button in this section; there is no second button of any kind.

limits.source: Skill 49 TY-3 (the signed close is up to 170 characters); the section also carries the support lines, so the cap is descriptive for the whole section

layout.desktop: Hero ground band, two columns inside the 1200 px content column. Left: the help line, one line saying how to reach help and carrying the support email address exactly as the approved copy prints it, and under it the one filled support button carrying the copy's own label. Right: the short signed note of thanks and the signature line, set in script. The support button is the only button in this section: no second button, no offer button and no price. No grey bar is drawn anywhere in this section, and no behaviour note names an element that is not drawn. Spacing and type: about 96 px of padding above and below the band, the two columns split roughly 50 and 50 with a 64 px gutter and both top-aligned. In the left column the help line is set at body size on up to three lines with the email address kept on one line and never broken; the filled support button sits 28 px under it, left-aligned, at least 48 px tall and sized to its label with generous horizontal padding, filled in the brand's primary colour with the label centred. In the right column the signed note is set in the brand script face at a display size on up to four lines, and the signature line sits 16 px under it in the same script face at a smaller size, left-aligned with the note. Light type on the hero ground keeps the brand's readable-contrast floor, and the band ends the page on a clean bottom edge: no footer link row, social row or newsletter strip is drawn inside it.
layout.mobile: Single-column phone stack: the signed note and its signature line in script first, then the help line carrying the support email address exactly as the approved copy prints it, and under it the one filled support button at full width. The support button is the only button in this section: no second button, no offer button and no price. No grey bar is drawn anywhere in this section, and no behaviour note names an element that is not drawn. Spacing and type: about 56 px of padding above and below the band with 20 px side gutters; the signed note leads at a display size in script on up to five lines with the signature line 12 px under it; 40 px of space separates the signature from the help line, which is set at body size with the email address on one line, and the button follows 24 px under the help line, at least 48 px tall and the full column wide. Readable contrast against the hero ground is kept, and the page ends at the band's bottom edge with no footer link row drawn inside it. Text handling: the signed note and the signature line are the only elements set in the script face, and every other word in the band uses the body face; the email address is never turned into a button or a second link row, and it stays plain selectable text. Left alignment is kept throughout, with the signature line aligned to the note's left edge.

sections.note: The one filled support button is the only button here; the band closes on the help line and the signed note; no offer button

wireframe.reference_note: The attached reference is a landing page sheet. For this page it gives the sheet grammar only: section chips with name tabs, printed type specs, labelled image plates, filled CTA chips and contiguous bands. Its sections, section count, words and layout are never copied.
wireframe.desktop_block: THANK-YOU DESKTOP — a five-section confirmation page, not a landing page. The sections are Confirmation and welcome, Order summary, Access, What happens next, Help manage and close, in that order, on alternating grounds with hard butt joins. The page carries exactly one image plate in total (in the first section). No section is an offer, a pitch or a persuasion band, and no filled button is an offer button. Never merge two numbered sections into one band.
wireframe.steps_block: STEPS — between four and six numbered steps, 1 up to the last step once each in that order, each beside its own step label from the copy, drawn in the client's design style (the DESIGN STYLE line governs the badge: square-cornered blocks in full-width rows for Style A, circles on a dotted line for Style B and C). Never a seventh step that the copy does not carry.
wireframe.do_not_copy: DO NOT COPY THE EXAMPLE'S MISTAKES — the style reference was drawn by a model for a landing page and carries flaws. Never reproduce: a misspelt label (DESKTOR for DESKTOP, BTEP for STEP, featofe, thwo); a section number printed twice or skipped; garbled badges; an invalid ratio such as 3:9; duplicated text; placeholder words such as lorem ipsum or GOES HERE; any landing-page section, pain band, benefit grid or founder letter that this page's copy does not carry.
